name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP off-site power lost and restored 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time in the war; no safety-system damage reported
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its last external power line, Ferosplavna-1, early on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators, the 27th total loss of off-site power in the war; the IAEA called the safety situation precarious and said the cause was unknown (Anadolu, 8 Nov; The Moscow Times, 8 Nov). Power was later restored. No damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the public reported. Repeated power losses at a plant in a war zone raise the chance of a more serious event; official updates come from the IAEA and national regulators.
rubric_hit: Plant lost all off-site power on 8 Nov (Watch); no safety-system damage or release (Alert not met)

sources.title: Anadolu — Ukraine's Zaporizhzhya nuclear plant loses all external power for 27th time: UN nuclear watchdog
The Moscow Times — Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Relying on Generators Again After Losing Internal Power Supply

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
